content: Induct on n=|X|. Necessity: a matching saturating X defines an injection m:X->Y, and m(S) is contained in N(S). Sufficiency: base n=0. If some nonempty proper A subset X is tight, |N(A)|=|A|, induction matches A into N(A). For the residual induced graph on X\A and Y\N(A), every T subset X\A has neighborhood N(T)\N(A), whose size is |N(A union T)|-|N(A)| at least |A union T|-|A|=|T|; induction matches the residual. If no nonempty proper subset is tight, each such T has |N(T)| at least |T|+1. Choose x in X and y in N({x}); after deleting x,y, each nonempty T subset X\{x} loses at most one neighbor and still has at least |T| neighbors. Induction gives a residual matching, to which xy is added.
